goal: the first 1-3 s stop the scroll
lesson: Make something move in the first 0.3 s of the hook (a pour, a drop, a head turn); a frozen face-off with a card popping in reads as a still.
evidence: scorecard rule 1 note: the first half-second is static; audience stopScroll 3/5

goal: a name viewers use for the ad
lesson: To give an ad a label viewers repeat, title the hook as a named situation (e.g. 'Sunday standoff'), then pair it with motion and the product so it also stops the scroll.
evidence: the simulated viewers referred to it as 'the Sunday standoff ad', yet stopScroll stayed 3/5

lesson: Put the brand name in the same frame and line as the key rule at the reveal and say it aloud before the end card; a clean plant/pulse/reveal/tag map alone left viewers remembering the rule, not the name.
when: products sold on a simple usage rule
evidence: scorecard rule 5 scored 5/5 but audience brandRecall 2/5

lesson: To make a usage rule stick, state it once as a short concrete line on screen and in the voice at the reveal (e.g. 'One capful per litre').
when: products with a dose or routine
evidence: the dose was the one thing every simulated viewer recalled and believed

lesson: Give the end card one purchase anchor (pack size and what it makes, where to buy, the price once set); without it click intent stays low.
evidence: audience clickIntent 2/5; viewers asked for size, price and stockist

goal: the product visibly causes the turn
lesson: Show the product's key action on screen as its own 1-2 s shot at the turn (the pour, the cap filling); telling it with a card leaves viewers asking how.
when: products used by an action (dosing, applying, pouring)
evidence: scorecard rule 4 note: the capful is never poured; viewers asked 'which cap, how much water?'

lesson: Give the main character one specific, visible detail of their own (a named pot, a sticky-note calendar) so they become someone, not a type.
evidence: scorecard rule 3 scored 3: no detail beyond the bun and the frown

lesson: Keep a claim's conditions in the on-screen wording (e.g. 'every two weeks, spring and summer'); a shortened rule reads as absolute and costs trust.
when: claims that depend on season, dose or use
evidence: audience trust 3/5: the season was missing from 'Every two weeks'

goal: a brief that passes the claims lint first time
lesson: Never write absolutes ('guaranteed') or pressure lines ('buy now or…') in the brief, not even in the noClaims list, phrase them as plain bans.
evidence: the brief needed a repair for 'Guaranteed' and 'buy now or'

goal: a bible that passes every check first time
lesson: Time every card at characters/15 + 1.5 s and every voice line at about 2.9 words per second before writing the shots, so lines never run into each other.
evidence: a repair for voice line l01 overrunning, then the animatic's reading-time check failed and the bible was redone

goal: the product's hero detail is visible at the reveal
lesson: At the reveal, keep cards in a top or bottom band clear of the product's hero detail (the cap, the label); the revised frames moved the card off the cap.
evidence: frame review: the yellow cap hid behind the 'One capful per litre' card; the revision fixed it

goal: varied coverage that reads without sound
lesson: Vary shot sizes and cut the hook and the turn faster (inserts of 0.5-1.2 s); a 20 s ad told in six similar medium frames feels static.
evidence: all six v1 shots were medium frames; scorecard rule 1 static opening; stopScroll 3/5

goal: the take keeps its own look, not the previz look
lesson: Never send a coloured previz still as the layout reference: Seedance copies its flat look; send a grey blockout marked CONTEXTUAL POSITIONING ONLY, and only when blocking matters.
evidence: s1_t02 copied the flat kit look; s1_t03 with the grey blockout kept the elements look

lesson: Use one approved full-body turnaround as the character reference; extra portraits generated separately drift from it and confuse the identity.
evidence: Juno portraits drifted from her turnaround; takes with the turnaround alone stayed consistent

goal: an exact product shape and colour in image sheets
lesson: To get the product exactly right in image-model sheets, give a Blender render of the product as the reference image; the model copies its shape and colours.
evidence: the Blender render fixed wrong Sprigly bottle sheets

goal: a second view of a place
lesson: To get a second angle of a place, ask for a reverse view from the approved plate; expect a wider angle of the same room rather than a true reverse, which still works as view 2.
evidence: kitchen reverse views came out as wider angles of the same room

goal: the lowest spend per approved shot
lesson: Draft every shot on Flash at 480p and re-run only the chosen draft on Seedance 2.5 at 720p with the same prompt, references and seed.
evidence: draft at about $0.27, final at $0.93, consistent with the draft

goal: every card readable and inside the safe zone
lesson: Start the end card at least 3.5 s before the end and place two-line cards at y ≥ 0.215; the redo that did this passed every check the first attempt failed.
evidence: attempt 1: readcheck FAIL on the end-card line and CTA, safe9x16 FAIL on two-line cards at y 0.20; attempt 2 with these changes passed all checks

goal: readable cards at a fast cut rate
lesson: When shots are shorter than a card's reading time, carry the same card (same id, text and position) across the consecutive shots instead of shortening the words.
evidence: the carried hook and rule cards passed the reading check across 1.2 s cuts

goal: the product visibly causes the turn
lesson: To make the product cause the turn on screen, give its key action its own short insert (about 1 s) right after the reveal, with the rule card held over it.
evidence: scorecard rule 4 rose from 4 to 5 with the capful insert

lesson: Pick the smallest pose that reads for a realisation beat; a big arms-up surprise breaks a calm, relieved tone.
evidence: both frame reviews and scorecard rule 6 flagged the arms-up surprise at the turn

lesson: Say the brand name inside the rule line at the reveal and frame the label as the ECU; this turned v1's perfect-but-forgettable map into a 5 with the name on screen.
when: products sold on a simple usage rule
evidence: rule 5 kept 5/5 while the name moved into the reveal frame and the voice ('the Sprigly cap')

lesson: Re-run the story stage (not only direction and bible) when the scorecard asks for a character detail; later stages cannot add identity on their own.
evidence: rule 3 stayed at 3 in v2 because the story stage was not re-run

lesson: Say the brand name inside the rule line at the reveal and show it on the product's key prop too; recall rose from 2 to 3 when the name moved into the reveal.
when: products sold on a simple usage rule
evidence: audience brandRecall 2/5 in v1, 3/5 in v2 after the name joined the rule; viewers still caught it late

goal: stop the viewers most likely to buy
lesson: To stop the guilt-prone buyer, open on the named failure ('Day 14. Still guessing.') but show the product by 1 s so the curiosity gap does not hide what is sold.
when: products that fix a small daily worry
evidence: the v2 simulation favoured the problem-first opening C for the guilt-prone segment, with viewers unsure what was sold until the reveal

lesson: Keep the payoff modest and the claim about the routine, not the result; 'one capful' reads as a promise to fix a dying plant when the payoff looks miraculous.
evidence: trust stayed 3/5 in both cuts; viewers doubted that 'a capful fixes it'

lesson: Keep the opening joke light rather than scolding; ad-weary viewers read guilt framing as 'guilt dressed up as a tip' and swipe.
evidence: ad-weary interviews in v2

lesson: When the owner stays generic, give the object of the problem a voice (a talking plant, a grumpy kettle): the second speaker turns narration into dialogue and lifted the character score from 3 to 4.
when: products for a thing the user cares for
evidence: Sprigly recreate scored 4 on rule 3 where v1 and v2 scored 3 with the same Juno

lesson: With a step bar at the top (y 0.14-0.20) put cards at y 0.285 or lower, and give every step at least 2.5 s; a 1.2 s step is gone before it is read.
evidence: frames review moved two cards under the bar; the scorecard flagged the 1.2 s STEP 2

lesson: In a wide with two characters, place the planted product beside the smaller character, never behind it; the fern's fronds hid the bottle in the hook.
when: voxel or 3D stages with plants or props in front
evidence: scorecard rule 5 dropped to 4 because the s1 bottle was covered

lesson: For Kokoro dialogue, prefer common words and full phrases: bm_george made 'sulking' sound like 'soaking', bm_lewis made 'glug' sound like 'glag', and a bare 'One capful. Per litre.' was heard as 'capsule'; 'So, one capful per litre.' passed.
evidence: four voice redos in the Sprigly recreate

lesson: Score 3D explainers on clarity, watch time and saves: the story-ad rules mark them down for having no character and a late product, which is the format working.
evidence: fern-water explainer 26/35 with rule 3 at 2 and rule 5 at 3 by design

lesson: In the cloud, render the explainer plate at 40 % with EEVEE 8 samples (about 12-15 s a frame on 4 cores); final quality belongs on a GPU.
evidence: the 15 s plate took about an hour on the cloud CPU
